clue.text: Lawyer on screen is a silk

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
a mask screens or hides the face

explanation.surface: A lawyer appearing on television is a silk, a senior barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silk' looks like the British senior barrister of the surface (a QC 'takes silk'), but here it is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a figured woven fabric, traditionally made of silk.

clue.text: Digital audiotape put down information in electronic form

parts.note: DAT is the standard abbreviation for digital audio tape
to abase someone is to humble or put them down

explanation.surface: Someone records a digital audiotape and then stores the information electronically.
explanation.definitionFit: A structured store of records held on a computer is exactly what this term names.

clue.text: Tiny isle's ballistic missile

parts.note: minute (pronounced my-NEWT) means very small
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, gives MAN

explanation.surface: A small island owns a ballistic missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minuteman is a long-serving American intercontinental ballistic missile.

clue.text: A learner following light carriage that's finally gone like a dream

indicators.note: the A and the learner come after the carriage, placed in that order
its last letter has gone, so the end of the word for the carriage is dropped

parts.note: a surrey is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
L is the learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A learner driver trails behind a vanished carriage, a dreamlike scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally gone' drops the last letter of the carriage word; 'following' places the A and learner after what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes the bizarre, irrational quality of dreams, as in Surrealist art.

clue.text: Marmite? Greater Manchester town's right out

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is put out of the town's name

parts.note: Stockport is a town in Greater Manchester, north-west England

explanation.surface: A question about the yeast spread followed by a remark that a Manchester town is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marmite' looks like the British yeast-extract spread, but here it is the French word for a cooking pot; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: In French a marmite is a large lidded cooking pot, the sort used for simmering stock.

clue.text: Novel performance by Mr Mackay perhaps

definitions.meaning: a novella by Henry James, the ghost story of 1898
Mr Mackay was the prison officer in the British sitcom Porridge; prison officers are called screws, so his act is a 'turn' by a screw

explanation.surface: A novel praised as a performance by a man called Mackay.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Mackay, played by Fulton Mackay in the 1970s BBC prison comedy Porridge, was a warder, slang 'screw'; a turn is a stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James wrote this famous ghost story; read as a phrase it also means a turn performed by a warder.

clue.text: Official document a hit perhaps

definitions.meaning: a formal grant of rights by a sovereign or state, such as a royal one
a hit record makes the charts, so jokingly it is something that charts

explanation.surface: An official document turns out to be a successful one.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal grant of rights is a formal document; whimsically, a record that charts is one too.

clue.text: Religious song about Saint's pre-eminence

indicators.note: the word for pre-eminence goes around the saint's letter

parts.note: the palm is the prize of victory, so 'bearing the palm' is being pre-eminent
S is the standard abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A hymn written about how a saint excels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms are the sacred songs of the Book of Psalms, sung in worship.

clue.text: Old masters neglecting one group of gods

indicators.note: leaving out one letter from the painters' name

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Old Master painter, so 'Titians' are his works
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Classic painters who overlooked a single member of a pantheon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were the older race of gods overthrown by Zeus and the Olympians.

clue.text: Police leader concerned with the person following suspect provides final irony

parts.note: Sting was the frontman of the rock band The Police
in can mean involved or concerned with, as in 'in property'
taken as written
a tail is someone who shadows a suspect

explanation.surface: A senior police officer tails a suspect, which ends in an ironic twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police leader' looks like a chief constable but is the singer Sting, leader of the band The Police.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names an unpleasant surprise or twist that comes right at the end.

clue.text: He produces sound of note

indicators.note: said aloud, the word for a banknote gives the entered letters

parts.note: a tenner is a British ten-pound note

explanation.surface: A man who makes a notable sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound of note' reads as notable music, but 'sound of' is the homophone signal on a tenner, British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with a high male voice is a man who produces musical tones.

clue.text: Nagging woman to call a great man? Not I

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it

indicators.note: the letter I is not wanted in the word for the great man

parts.note: a giant is a man of great stature or achievement

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to call a nagging woman a great man, and denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing, quarrelsome woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Have beer with Northern bird

parts.note: bitter is a British style of hoppy draught beer

explanation.surface: Drinking a pint of beer with a northern bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is the classic British pub beer; 'bird' is in Britain slang for a woman, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like marsh bird known for its booming call.

clue.text: Military group holding test's overthrown old empire

indicators.note: the whole combination is turned over and read backwards
the alliance's letters go around the test's letters

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles

explanation.surface: A military alliance holds a test and an old empire falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the test inside the alliance, and 'overthrown' turns the whole thing backwards. The MOT is the yearly British vehicle safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire, centred on Turkey, lasted from about 1300 until 1922.

clue.text: Pestilent miser arranged profit from saving

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A nasty miser fixed up a return on savings.
explanation.definitionFit: This is interest paid only on the original principal, a return earned by savers.

clue.text: Extravagant roll could give man bruise

indicators.note: wild or extravagant handling of the letters jumbles them

explanation.surface: An over-elaborate bread roll could leave a man bruised.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a reverse anagram: an extravagant (rearranged) form of the answer could give MAN BRUISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is a long bread roll filled as a sandwich, a sub.

clue.text: Apartment building with temporary accommodation sheltering European chaps

indicators.note: the tent's letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay
chaps are men

explanation.surface: An apartment block with a tent housing European men.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, especially a run-down one.

clue.text: You need to make better infernal precocious child

indicators.note: the solver must make something new from the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Advice that you must improve a hellish, precocious child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make better' reads as improve, but 'You need to make' is the anagram signal on BETTER INFERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means a 'terrible child', for a precocious or shocking person.

clue.text: Case holding uranium for sale

indicators.note: the word for case contains the uranium symbol

parts.note: a legal case is an action in court
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A box containing uranium is up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Authentic nonsense served up by American estate agent

parts.note: real means genuine or authentic

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: An American estate agent dishes out genuine nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtor is the US term for a real-estate agent, a trademark of its national association.

clue.text: Firm's team of workers?

definitions.meaning: steady, secure and not easily moved
the team of racehorses or of people working for one employer, playfully horses as workers

explanation.surface: A firm's team of workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and firm; it also names a group of horses, riders or staff under one owner.

clue.text: One finds in theatre a clear sentimentality

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone notices in the theatre a clear excess of sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is used figuratively for cloying, sugary sentiment.

clue.text: Bird to feel bad about taking off first

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken off

parts.note: to regret something is to feel bad about it

explanation.surface: A bird feels bad about taking off first.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron with fine breeding plumes.

clue.text: Daily, comedian Edmondson shows example of absurd behaviour

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day, also a char
Ade Edmondson is a British comedian from The Young Ones and Bottom

explanation.surface: Each day the comedian Edmondson shows silly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb but is a noun: a cleaning lady, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a farcical show put on to keep up appearances.

clue.text: Bounder in grip of writer's block

indicators.note: held tight inside the writer's name

parts.note: J M Barrie was the Scottish author of Peter Pan
a cad and a bounder are both dishonourable men

explanation.surface: A scoundrel gripped by writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' looks like a phrase but splits: 'writer's' gives BARRIE and 'block' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a barrier that blocks a way, so it is a block.

clue.text: Offal after time is strong-smelling

indicators.note: the strong-smelling word comes after the time letter

parts.note: ripe means pungent, smelly

explanation.surface: Offal that has gone smelly after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle or sheep, eaten as offal.

clue.text: Snare fish after net's repaired

indicators.note: the fishing word comes after the rearranged net
a mended net is put back together in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fisher tries to trap fish once the net has been mended.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to catch or snare something in a tangle.

clue.text: Religious leader investigates head of Trinity

parts.note: pries means probes or snoops into

indicators.note: the first letter of the college name

explanation.surface: A churchman investigates the master of Trinity College.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest leads worship and religious rites.
